steps.description: Filter to genes with at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size) as a minimal pre-filter — do not over-filter, since DESeq2's independent filtering does the rest. Set the condition factor with an explicit reference level (control) and fit DESeq2 with design ~condition; run the Wald test for the contrast condition_treated_vs_control. In parallel, fit edgeR's quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and the same design as a robustness cross-check. Shrink the DESeq2 log2 fold change with apeglm (single-coefficient contrast). Apply Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment with DESeq2's independent filtering at alpha=0.05; do not filter by raw p-value or by fold-change alone. Before trusting the adjusted p-values, inspect the raw p-value histogram for the expected uniform/left-skewed shape. Report the number of genes tested after filtering, the number with padj<0.05, the number of genes flagged as count outliers (Cook's distance, NA p-values) given n=3 per group, and report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap (intersection = high-confidence set; method-specific genes = secondary set). Produce MA plot and dispersion plot as fit diagnostics.

plan.title: Liver 3v3 treated vs control DE with power caveat + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12000 x 7 raw gene-level Salmon counts (human liver, drug treatment) with metadata for 3 treated vs 3 control samples, unpaired, single batch. Track 1 runs sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) to check the treated/control samples separate and no outlier or batch structure confounds the comparison, then fits DESeq2 (median-of-ratios normalization inside the model, explicit control-as-reference factor level, Wald test on ~condition) with an edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check on the same counts/design for robustness, apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control log2 fold change, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05. Because the design has only 3 replicates per group, the differential_expression step is flagged by the knowledge base (R-0017/R-0094/R-0162): both count models recover only a minority of true DE genes at this replicate depth, mostly the larger-effect ones, so an absent gene is not evidence of no change, and the report must state expected power and not loosen the FDR threshold to compensate. Track 2 takes the full ranked gene list (DESeq2 Wald statistic, not fold-change or p-value alone, per the disputed-rule choice stated here) into fgsea preranked GSEA against the locally staged MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways as secondary collections, each with its own release stated and size window 15-500, since with only 3v3 replicates a fixed count of significant genes may fall under the ~50-gene floor needed for a sound over-representation test — a full-list ranked test does not have that floor. The final report step consolidates DE tables (unshrunken and shrunken LFC, SE, padj), fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, the GSEA leading-edge tables per collection, and the reproducibility record (session info, package versions, seed, gene-set collection versions).
